articles.title: In Week 6’s ‘Reacts’ poll, Chiefs fans want to see more Cyrus Allen
articles.summary: Sign up here to join SB Nation NFL Reacts.﻿
articles.body:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here .

And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation.

Chiefs Kingdom's confidence level hasn't dipped below 89% since the team whooped up on the Denver Broncos in Week 1. There was a one-point percentage drop in confidence frmo Week 5 to Week 6, however.

Over three-fourths of Chiefs fans who voted in this poll want to see more playing time for wide receiver Cyrus Allen than for running back Emmett Johnson or defensive back Jadon Canady.

Here were some of the best comments from the Arrowhead Pride community:

EJ I love that K-9 is running wild but damn I want to save some of that energy for the playoffs and not run him into the ground by playing him all the time. Unless we are behind and need him.

I want to see more of both Johnson and Allen. I picked Johnson though. He already is and has some expectations to carry some of the load. I am indeed excited about Cyrus Allen, he had some great touches in preseason. That said, he was 5 or 6 on the depth chart for a reason of those above my pay grade. His need to shine now is due to injury.

I would be most interested/excited to see more of Allen, but I put Emmett Johnson, since Kenneth Walker needs to not average 25 touches per game if we hope the Chiefs' season will be 20 or 21 games.

I think Allen will get more targets as the season goes on. If I remember correctly Rice wasn't used much early on, but the 2nd half of the season was when he made most of is plays.

Want to see Allen, but Johnson is the more important need in reducing Walker's touches. Allen isn't going to change the result of the season but using up Walker will directly impact the playoffs.

Click here to see other recent survey results.

articles.title: Badgers bounce back from loss to Nebraska with sweep
articles.summary: The Badgers got a sweep in their return to the Field House.
articles.body:
Coming off their loss to the No. 1 Nebraska Cornhuskers, the No. 6 Wisconsin Badgers took care of business at home, beating the Maryland Terrapins 25-18, 25-23, 25-18 in a sweep of their own.

Wisconsin fought hard in the Nebraska loss, and head coach Kelly Sheffield was pleased with his team's performance afterwards. Even with the loss, the Badgers moved back up to No. 6 in the AVCA Top 25, as Florida fell two spots to No. 7.

Wisconsin opened the first set on a 6-1 run, quickly setting the tone as Lynney Tarnow, Eva Travis, and Decelise Champion all got kills. From there, the Badgers never really got into trouble in the first set, and a kill from Champion got them the finish at 25-18.

It was a clean set from Wisconsin, which had 15 kills and only three attack errors, as they hit .500 in the opening frame.

The second set was the closest of the three, as it was Maryland that got out to an early 7-5 lead. But the Badgers went on another 6-1 run, thanks to a pair of kills from Champion, a kill from Travis, and a trio of attack errors on Maryland.

From there, the set was back-and-forth, with the Terrapins even taking a 21-18 lead late on the verge of tying things up at one a piece. But the Badgers rallied to rattle off six straight points before closing the set 25-23 after Maryland brought things to within one. This time, it was a Charlie Fuerbringer kill to seal the deal and put Wisconsin up 2-0.

The third set was close in the early going, with both sides tied at 5. But the Badgers went on a 5-1 run, creating some distance, and they were in control the rest of the set, even when the Terrapins provided some resistance. Wisconsin went on an 8-2 run to go up 18-10, and the Terrapins never got within six, as the Badgers got the sweep with a 25-18 win in the third set.

Wisconsin out-hit Maryland .344 to .155, and Decelise Champion finished with 17 kills and five blocks. Lynney Tarnow also had eight blocks, while Charlie Fuerbringer had 35 assists. Anna Bardaro added 15 digs as well, as she and Kristen Simon both played well.

The Badgers will take on the Iowa Hawkeyes next on Sunday, with first serve set for 1:00 p.m. on Big Ten Network.

articles.title: Golden State Valkyries hold on for WNBA Finals Game 1 victory over Atlanta Dream
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — The “defense wins championships” crowd will have a new case study to evaluate after the best-of-seven WNBA Finals series between the Golden S...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The "defense wins championships" crowd will have a new case study to evaluate after the best-of-seven WNBA Finals series between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream wraps.

The Valkyries had the best defensive rating during the regular season, while the Dream were third. The Dream led the league in steals per game, while the Valkyries were fourth. The series, as a result, will come down to which team can maintain composure and win the possession battle. In Game 1 on Saturday afternoon, the Valkyries answered the bell with a 68-64 win against the fourth-seeded Dream.

Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points, while Allisha Gray returned from a hand injury to lead the Dream with 19 points.

The Dream will try to even the series Monday at the Chase Center.

articles.title: Army football's Cale Hellums drawing comparisons to Bryson Daily
articles.summary: Army football's Cale Hellums drawing comparisons to Bryson Daily after 5-TD game vs FAU.
articles.body:
Check out our Army football vs FAU photo gallery, best images

Samari Howard received a sideline apology.

Cale Hellums was in a giving mood following Saturday's 56-24 rout of Florida Atlantic , and why not? Army's senior quarterback has a lot of good fortune to spread around.

The parallels between Hellums and Daily are becoming more clear every week. Daily took over as starter as a junior in 2023 and blossomed during a 12-2 senior campaign in 2024, posting a nation-high 32 rushing touchdowns and finishing sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.

Hellums learned much under Daily and became his heir apparent in 2025. Running the same offense and showing the same drive and spirit, Hellums guided Army to a Fenway Bowl victory, and now has the Black Knights (4-2) just two wins from another bowl berth.

And now Hellums and Daily share a line in the Army record books. Hellums rushed for five touchdowns against Florida Atlantic , tying the Academy record set by Daily nearly two years earlier to the day in a five-TD effort against East Carolina in 2024.

"Bryson's a great friend of mine,'' Hellums said. "He was an awesome teammate and someone that I looked up to when I was playing behind him.''

Hellums great in red zone for Army football

Hellums said he had no idea at the time that he had tied Daily's mark with an extra-effort 1-yard score early in the fourth quarter against FAU – he did know he already had four because when he followed fullback Jake Rendina into the end zone from 3 yards out late in the third. He paused in the end zone and counted out 1, 2, 3, 4 on his hand to celebrate.

Of the record-tying tally, "To be able to match that is pretty cool,'' Hellums said. "Definitely the competitor in me wanted to beat it, but I'll send (Daily) a funny text.''

What's also funny and heart-warming was his sideline reaction following the fourth score. On the play previous, split back Samari Howard went into motion, received the short "flip'' pass off the snap and got a hard 2 yards when he needed three. Hellums tried to go over the top on the next play, rolled left off his line and a defender and reached back, stretching the ball over the goal line. It was initially ruled a stop by the officials, but a video review showed Hellums had gotten the score.

In a conversation heard on the sidelines, Hellums apologized to Samari over getting the score (not to worry, because Howard produced the game's first touchdown on a 30-yard pitch play from Hellums just 21 seconds in).

For the most part, Hellums tries to remain even-keeled on the field, but he showed off a "lean at the tape' – much like a sprinter at the finish line – as he completed a 58-yard burst off the left side early in the first quarter, matching a score of equal career-best length a week earlier against Tulane.

This season, Hellums has 13 rushing touchdowns and 719 yards on 129 carries; last season, he had 18 rushing scores, and 1,223 yards on 304 carries. For his career (which includes a few appearances in relief in 2024), Hellums has 31 rushing scores and 1,970 yards on 450 carries.

Hellums had two rushing scores in the opener against Bryant, three in the win at Temple and two against Tulane. Hellums' 25-carry effort against FAU (netting 195 yards) comes a week after posting 38 carries and a career-high 223 yards vs. Tulane, the 11th-best rushing effort in Army history.

"He's certainly playing much better this year than he did a year ago,'' praised Army head coach Jeff Monken. "And, much like Bryson Daily during his junior year, has some games where it was really a struggle and didn't play as well as he would have liked. His senior year (Daily) played much better. ... It comes with experience and comes with the confidence of getting that experience.

"He (Hellums) also knows that he's our quarterback, which is kind of where he was a year ago, even at this point. So I think just that growth and maturity and he's just playing well, taking care of the ball - that's the most important thing that he's done.''
authors: Ken McMillan, Middletown Times Herald- Record

articles.title: Texas football: Steve Sarkisian doesn't rule out benching Arch Manning after Florida loss
articles.summary: At the beginning of this season, Arch Manning was considered among the top quarterbacks in the country. But the Texas football team's 27-24 loss at home to F...
articles.body:
At the beginning of this season, Arch Manning was considered a Heisman Trophy front-runner and one of the top quarterbacks in the country. But after the second-year starter again struggled in Texas football's 27-24 loss at home to unranked Florida on Saturday, is it time for a change?

Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian wouldn't rule it out after the game. After the stunning setback , Sarkisian was asked if he had thought about making a change at quarterback. Sarkisian answered, "I just felt like we didn't play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now. So everything is going to be evaluated."

Does the evaluation of everything include Manning's job status?

"Everything means everything," Sarkisian bluntly stated.

Sarkisian was later again asked about Manning's performance. He said there was plenty of blame to go around for Saturday's loss. As a team, Texas collected 272 yards and had just four drives go longer than five plays. In the third quarter, UT gained eight yards while running four plays.

"It'd be easy for me to say, 'Hey, Arch was the problem today.' Was Arch perfect? No, but nobody was perfect on offense today," Sarkisian said. "We took turns today, and that's where I have to look at every aspect of what we're doing because if it was one person, it'd be easy. Yeah, change one guy and everything's going to be great. Well, I don't think that that was all the issue today. Could he have been better? No doubt about it. But there's some other issues that need to be addressed."

Texas, No. 7 in the Associated Press poll, will surely slip when the new rankings are released Sunday. Texas (4-2, 1-2) will attempt to snap its two-game losing streak next week at home against Ole Miss.

Arch Manning, Texas offense have surprising struggles against Florida

Against a Florida secondary that ranked last in the SEC (and 131st among 138 FBS-level teams) in passing yardage by allowing 268.7 yards per game, Manning threw for just 173 yards and a touchdown while completing 14 of his 20 passes. A 62-yard connection with Emmett Mosley V while Texas was trailing by 10 points in the fourth quarter accounted for around 35% of Manning's yardage total.

Manning didn't throw an interception, but he did lose a costly fumble while taking a sack on UT's final drive and he was dropped for a loss on another fourth-down attempt in the fourth quarter. Last week, Manning threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter that led to 10 points in a 27-24 loss to Oklahoma .

"We talk about winning the fourth quarter, and we didn't do that today," Manning said. "Moving forward, we've got to win the fourth."

When told afterward about Sarkisian's evaluation comment, Manning said "everyone's evaluated every week. That's how it is at a school like this. Elite players, so everyone's got to get better, and it starts with me."

Through six games, Manning has thrown for 1,295 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions while completing 63.9% of his passes. He's leading an offense that has yet to score more than 24 points against a Power Four defense.

Texas has not wholly benched its starting quarterback for a non-injury reason since Sarkisian's first season in 2021 when Casey Thompson replaced Hudson Card after a disastrous September defeat at Arkansas. Behind Manning on the Texas depth chart are sophomore KJ Lacey and freshman Dia Bell . Both were highly-rated recruits, but Lacey has thrown only nine passes in his college career while Bell has yet to get into a game at Texas.

images.caption: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) leaves the field after the 27-24 loss to Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman)

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian on the Texas offense: ‘I have to evaluate everything’
articles.summary: “I'm probably harder on myself than anybody and I'll evaluate this game the same way."
articles.body:
AUSTIN — After a stunning 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators in which the No. 7 Texas Longhorns only ran 19 plays for 96 yards in the second half — 62 0f which came on a desperation heave on 4th and 7 down 10 points with five minutes left in the game — head coach Steve Sarkisian said that he's going to have a long night.

The Longhorns had already had a long day.

Did he think of making a change away from struggling senior quarterback Arch Manning, who missed too many open receivers, took too many sacks, and committed another game-changing turnover when he fumbled on a sack with two minutes remaining and the Longhorns down three points?

"I just felt like we didn't we play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now, so everything is going to be evaluated," Sarkisian said.

What happened to the offense after scoring 10 points on the first two drives?

"Failure to to do our job well, not calling good enough plays, not winning one on ones," Sarkisian said. "I mean, it's all of it. That's my point. It's like, I have to evaluate everything."

What were Sarkisian's impressions of how Manning played? When he says everything is evaluated, does that include…

"Everything means everything," Sarkisian interrupted.

How do does Sarkisian balance changing personnel versus improving the personnel the Longhorns are already using?

"That's part of the evaluation. We need to figure that out," Sarkisian said.

After all the effort put into this season, why are things not clicking and heading in this direction?

"No, that's the frustrating part, and the frustrating part is we practice really well," Sarkisian said. "We're in a great frame of mind to go execute, and we're not, and so that's part of the evaluation. I've got to look at it all to figure out where is the disconnect."

"I think details and route running, I think pass protection, picking up blitzes, I think not being able to run the ball for two yards in short yardage, just to name a few that pop into my head," Sarkisian said.

What changes has Sarkisian made to his play calling or has he stuck to his base offense over the last three games? Does he anticipate making…

"We're going to evaluate everything," Sarkisain said, interrupting another reporter. "I don't know how many times I need to say we're going to evaluate everything from an offensive perspective. Part of that is play call."

What process will Sarkisian use to evaluate himself as a play caller?

"The process is the same process that I use every weekend. I evaluate everything that we do, from the game plan itself to the play calls themselves to who was touching the ball to how did we block to what do we call in specific situations to how did every individual perform, myself included," Sarkisian said.

"I don't take it personally evaluating myself — I'm probably harder on myself than anybody and I'll evaluate this game the same way. I'm sure there's going to be situations I'm going to be really hard on myself because we weren't good enough."

Sarkisian speaks frequently about not concerning himself with what people outside the football facility think, but if he wants to challenge the assertion that he's harder on himself than anybody else, taking a look at social media might give him a different perspective on that.

articles.title: Florida football coach Jon Sumrall trolls Texas after Gators upset Longhorns
articles.summary: Florida head coach Jon Sumrall trolled Texas after Saturday's win.
articles.body:
Florida pulled off a massive upset over No. 7 Texas in Austin on Saturday.

The Gators walked into Austin and beat the Longhorns 27-24, improving to 5-2 overall. Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning struggled again, throwing for 173 yards and one touchdown, while not seeing the field very well.

He also fumbled at the end of the fourth quarter, giving the Gators the ball back, and they never gave it back to the Longhorns.

After the game, Gators head coach Jon Sumrall trolled the Longhorns by wearing a cowboy hat as he was walking out of the stadium.

A massive win for Jon Sumrall and the Gators

Sep 19, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall watches his team warm up before the game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Saturday's win snapped a two-game losing streak for the Gators after they started the season with a perfect 4-0 record. They now have serious momentum going into their next game against the Georgia Bulldogs on Halloween.

Gators quarterback Tramell Jones finished the game with 155 yards through the air and two touchdowns, while also rushing for 41 yards. It was the first start of his career since Aaron Philo is dealing with an injury.

Considering how well Jones played on Saturday, he may be in line for another start against the Bulldogs, even if Philo is ready to return.

articles.title: No. 1 Ferris State football overcomes early deficit to beat No. 1 GVSU
articles.summary: Another epic Anchor Bone Classic is in the books. It lived up to the hype.
articles.body:
ALLENDALE - Top-ranked Ferris State trailed early but quickly turned things around against No. 13 Grand Valley State.

The Bulldogs snagged an interception and a fumble in the second quarter to erase a 17-point deficit and propel them to a 41-34 win over the Lakers in the Anchor Bone Classic on Saturday, Oct. 17, at Lubbers Stadium in Allendale.

Wyatt Bower scored on a 3-yard run early in the second quarter. Zak Ahearn scored on a 10-yard run before Jay Cady kicked a 25-yard field goal. FSU put in its other kicker, Eoin O'Sullivan, who nailed a 46-yard field goal putting the Bulldogs up 20-17 at halftime.

Bower started the third quarter with a 16-yard touchdown run, then threw a 32-yard scoring strike to Tae Boyd to make it 34-17.

The Lakers, who held a 17-0 early lead, didn't score again until 54 seconds remaining in the third quarter when Andrew Schuster threw his third touchdown pass of the game, a 61-yard strike to Kellen Reed.

But a field goal and a Schuster TD pass to Kellen Russell-Dixon pulled the Lakers within 41-34 with 4:17 to go.

This is a developing story and will be updated with details and reaction.

articles.title: WATCH: Texas A&M HC provides update on junior wide receiver
articles.summary: Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko said the Aggies are supporting and praying for Ashton Bethel-Roman, amid his absence for personal matters.
articles.body:
It wasn't all good news for Texas A&M football after a 41-0 shutout win on Saturday , as head coach Mike Elko provided an update on the Aggies ' talented junior wide receiver.

Ashton Bethel-Roman did not attend Saturday's home contest against The Citadel due to personal reasons and is being "given space" by the team to deal with the matter. This comes after Bethel-Roman dealt with an injury earlier in the year, before making a return back to the lineup recently.

He was named the starter at the beginning of the season, but has caught just seven passes for 56 yards in five games played through the first seven weeks. Bethel Roman has been targeted 15 times in 2026, which is fourth among the wide receiving corps, behind Isaiah Horton, Mario Craver and Aaron Gregory.

Here's Elko's update on Bethel-Roman in the postgame press conference via TexAgs :

Texas A&M's wideout group keeps getting lighter each week. Terry Bussey and Madden Williams are out for the year and Mario Craver, Marcel Reed's top target, has also seen limited action over recent weeks while dealing with an injury. Fortunately, rising stars like Gregory and TK Norman stepped up for the Aggies in their Week 7 shutout of The Citadel, hauling in 11 combined receptions for 182 yards and two touchdowns.

Bethel-Roman being out of the rotation is a massive hit for Elko and company. With multiple huge SEC contests rapidly approaching, the health and overall status of Texas A&M's offense, especially the wide receiving corps, could be detrimental moving forward.

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes and opinions. Follow Dylan on X: @ dylanmflippo .

articles.title: Daniel Dubois destroys Fabio Wardley in blistering fashion to fulfil rematch vow
articles.summary: Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel, five months on from being criticised for not pulling his man out against Dubois in the first match
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois left no doubt in the mind as he knocked out Fabio Wardley inside two rounds, fulfilling his vow to make quick work of his British heavyweight rival in their rematch.

Having been the one to succumb to an early knockdown in the first matchup, Dubois came out of the blocks in blistering fashion and sent Wardley to the canvas inside 17 seconds.

Wardley, weathering a first-round firestorm, attempted to respond with a huge right cross of his own up against the ropes which narrowly missed.

But Dubois continued to pummel his rival and threatened to put him away as the round came to a close, Wardley's trainer Ben Davison holding the towel seemingly ready to pull his man out before the Ipswich man was saved by the bell.

The punishment continued as the second round began, rocking Wardley with a sharp one-two before he was forced into a corner once again, with Dubois's attacks overwhelming his British rival.

This time Davison did throw in the towel, something he was criticised for not doing in the first fight , to seal Wardley's fate and ensure Dubois retained his world title.

"Shout out to everybody, shoutout to my dad, my whole team. Fabio is a great warrior, but it was my time, my era," Dubois said.

"I had bad intentions from the beginning. Our back was against the wall first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight."

Wardley is now left to bounce back from two consecutive losses having entered the year undefeated.

He said: "It's never fun to lose. It is what it is, I've always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around, there's no shame in testing yourself against the best.

"Daniel is testament to coming again and I'll come again. You come with a game plan, try to adjust things and it didn't work tonight. It's credit to Daniel of how well he prepared."

Wardley came into the mammoth heavyweight rematch off the back of a brutal defeat in the British pair's first meeting back in May, when he failed to take advantage of two early knockdowns before Dubois showed immense heart, turning the tide and eventually stopping Wardley in the 11th round.

The 31-year-old Ipswich man was left battered and bloodied by the time the referee eventually waved off the clash at Manchester's Co-op Live, his nose smashed in and right eye near-completely shut. There was criticism of his corner, chiefly trainer Ben Davison, for not throwing in the towel earlier.

Wardley, however, told promoter Frank Warren of his desire to rematch Dubois immediately following the first bout , revealing this request was made in his dressing room before leaving the arena.

Wardley was insistent that he was in a better position to make adjustments from the first bout compared to Dubois, saying that the room for growth was "exponentially in my favour", despite being the older man by two years.

Dubois was the heavier man on the night by a slender margin of five pounds, though both fighters took to the scale at career-heaviest weights at Friday's ceremonial weigh-in in London's Old Spitalfields Market.

And despite Wardley's confidence, Dubois put on an emphatic display to finish his British rival in short order, taking a step towards his goal of becoming undisputed champion at heavyweight.

Dubois has already fought and failed in the pursuit of undisputed gold, knocked out by Oleksandr Usyk under the Wembley arch in July 2025, his previous fight before facing Wardley earlier this year.

He is now looks set to target another heavyweight champion after Usyk vacated his titles earlier this year, and squared off with IBF holder Filip Hrgovic - who stunted British 21-year-old Moses Itauma's stunning rise in August - in the ring after his second triumph over Wardley.
